verdicts.own_cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ResourceManager.as:41,:186,:205,:207,:213 + my own decrypt of all five blobs under reference/extracted/android/
verdicts.reason: Every quoted line is verbatim at the stated number, and I reproduced the result myself rather than taking it on trust. ResourceManager.as:41 lists the five filenames; :186 'ba = decryptByteArray(ba,resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1));' - so the key IS the second character, per resource. I ran the algorithm from :205-213 (i=3..255, swap ba[i]<->ba[i+256] when i%11==0, then ba[i]^=key) on all five blobs with the derived keys and every one inflated to a valid SWF: 115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin key 104 -> CWS ver 17, 1,040,849 inflated bytes, 1,912 SymbolClass entries (the finding's exact numbers); 113_MusicResource key 117 -> ver 17, 1,402,677 B, 13 symbols; 122_SoundResource key 111 -> ver 17, 29,623 B, 13 symbols (matches C3); 124_ImageResource key 109 -> ver 17, 1,908,229 B, 85 symbols (matches C1's 109); 120_BGResource key 103 -> ver 17, 4,412,340 B, 67 symbols. The 'CWS magic survives' explanation also checks out: bytes 0-2 are untouched by the loop, and byte 3 of 115 is 0x79 which XORs with 104 to exactly 17, the SWF version. Strongest finding in the packet.

REFUTED on its central causal claim and on its lane_impact, both of which I falsified first-hand. (1) 'The web build REPLACED that hover affordance with a persistent on-bar notice' is false. The web build KEEPS the hover affordance verbatim: §1t113s0§.as:241-242 add MOUSE_OVER/MOUSE_OUT on §1t5158s0§ bound to §1t5215s0§/§1t5216s0§, whose bodies at :542-543 and :548-549 set '§1t5161s0§.visible = true/false' plus the bust highlight - the exact android shape. The packet's own sibling finding ui-hud/the-change-stance-affordance-IS-the-portrait-bust-not-a-separate-button states this correctly, so the two contradict each other and this one is the wrong half. (2) THE FRAME WINS, and it agrees: I cropped B_t851.867 and looked - a v0.717 duel HUD showing the bust with a BLUE stance ring and the words 'CHANGE STANCE' rendered right under it. The hover tooltip is live in the web build. (3) The 'because' is a conflation of two different strings. The rollover label is getString(208), and strings.json["208"] resolves to 'Change Stance' - it is PRESENT in the v0.682 table. String 960 is a different string on a different widget. So 960's absence cannot be 'because the android label is a portrait rollover'; the real reason is the one the packet's other finding gives correctly - android's updateReload (BattleUI.as:259-263) has no ratio==0 branch, so no code path would ever request 960. (4) The lane_impact is actively harmful: 'build the WEB behaviour ... not the android hover tooltip' would delete a widget the web build demonstrably ships and a v0.717 frame demonstrably shows. WHAT SURVIVES, and is already carried by the sibling findings: android :262 is the entire reload-bar text logic; android has no empty-state bar label; strings.json has no key '960'; and the web rescales (reload-48)/(max-48) inside §1t5205s0§ while android passes a pre-normalised percentage.

Verified line by line, and this is the CORRECT explanation of string 960 - the one its sibling finding gets wrong. Android BattleUI.as:259-263 updateReload is exactly two statements: :261 'this.reloadbar.bar.scaleX = percentage;' :262 'this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;'. No ratio==0 branch, no second htmlText, so no android code path could ever request 960 - which is why strings.json (2,533 entries, the v0.682 table) returns None for '960' while returning 'Change Stance' for '208' and 'Critical Hit' for '175'. The web twin §1t113s0§.as:326-359 is a full three-state machine: :328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' clamped at :329-332, :336-343 grey §1t5204s0§ at _loc3_==0, :344-347 hidden for 0<r<1, :348-358 black §1t5203s0§ plus '§1t1516s0§("Snd_criticalDamage")' at r>=1. The two htmlText constants are built at :110-111 with getString(175) at '#000000' and getString(960) at '#BBBBBB'. The lane_impact's cross-reference also checks: §1t99s0§.as:3050 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;'. And I saw the label render: my frame_0020 crop shows a GREY 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' sitting on the third track, matching the #BBBBBB empty-state branch. new_findings.text: Found while judging skills-meters/the-web-build-seeds-stance-mastery-at-1. The stance slash-length formulas DIVERGE between builds, and the 'Light x0.54' figure in circulation is mislabelled - 0.54 is HEAVY. Web v0.717 (§1t99s0§.as, switch at :3091): Light case §1t12220s0§ :3094 is a FLAT 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4' with NO mastery term at all; Balanced §1t12221s0§ :3105 is '§1t4420s0§ * (1 + 0.2 * §1t4422s0§ * 0.1)' = x1.02 at mastery 1; Heavy §1t12222s0§ :3116 is '§1t4420s0§ * (0.5 + 0.4 * §1t4423s0§ * 0.1)' = x0.54 at mastery 1, floored at 100 px by :3117-3120. Android v0.682 (MCSPlayer.as setStance :3027): LIGHT :3030 'baseSlashLength * 1.5'; BALANCED :3041 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'; HEAVY :3052 '(0.5 + 0.5 * heavyMastery * 0.01)' floored at 100 by :3053-3056. So THREE things differ: the Light constant (1.4 web vs 1.5 android), the Balanced mastery coefficient (0.2*0.1=0.02 vs 0.5*0.01=0.005), and the Heavy coefficient (0.04 vs 0.005) - a 4x-8x difference in how much mastery buys. §1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ are pinned to balancedMastery/heavyMastery by MCSPlayer.as:182's named signature via the initPlayer argument bridge. There is also a fourth web case §1t12224s0§ at :3130-3131 with a flat *1.4 (android's REVERSED_STANCE, :3067, is *1.5).
new_findings.quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3094 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;' vs android MCSPlayer.as:3030 'this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5;' · web :3116 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4423s0§ * 0.1);' vs android :3052 'this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * (0.5 + 0.5 * this.heavyMastery * 0.01);'
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: any stance reach number must be taken from the WEB formulas, and 'Light x0.54' must be relabelled HEAVY x0.54 wherever it appears - web Light carries no mastery scaling whatsoever, so mastery buys reach only in Balanced and Heavy. Another dated C2 divergence with numbers.

new_findings.text: Found while checking the mis-ranged third example in nf-judge/name-greps-over-the-web-payload-are-not-evidence-of-absence. The web v0.717 Item class carries EIGHT modifier constants where android v0.682 carries five. Web §1t17s0§.as:8-16 maps one-for-one onto android Item.as:8-16 (80/81/82/89/125 = PCOLORMODID/SCOLORMODID/USESMODID/NAMEMODID/CREATORMODID), but web :18-22 adds §1t8739s0§=206, §1t8740s0§=207, §1t8741s0§=208 with no android counterpart - android's constant block ends at :18 'USEPROCGENNAME' and :20 begins the instance fields. Confirmed by grep: 'grep -nE "= *20[678];" reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/Item.as' returns zero hits. So itemdata modifier ids 206/207/208 are a web-side addition, and any item-modifier table ported from the android build is missing three modifier kinds.

new_findings.lane_impact: L?/items: three modifier ids (206, 207, 208) exist only in v0.717. Do not treat an android-derived modifier list as complete, and re-check the 412 <modifier> rows in itemdata.xml (an ANDROID artifact per C2) for whether 206/207/208 appear at all.

new_findings.text: Qualifies ui-hud/the-change-stance-button-is-the-portrait-bust-itself without refuting it. The stancecolor1 frame index is 1/2/3 as that finding says, but it is NOT one-to-one with stance: android MCSPlayer.as's setStance switch calls setStanceColor(2) from BOTH BALANCED_STANCE (:3048) and REVERSED_STANCE (:3074), and setStanceColor(3) from BOTH HEAVY_STANCE (:3063) and DUAL_STANCE (:3089). Five stances, three ring frames. Web §1t99s0§.as's switch has the same shape with a fourth case §1t12224s0§ at :3130. So a rebuild that infers the player's stance from the ring colour will be wrong in Reversed and Dual, and the ring is a three-value display, not a stance readout.
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: ship the ring as a 3-frame display driven by setStanceColor, not as a stance readout; and never infer stance from ring colour in a frame study - blue/tan/red cannot separate Balanced from Reversed or Heavy from Dual.
